title: Sara Duterte can best answer allegations, says House prosecutor
summary: House lead impeachment prosecutor Representative Gerville Luistro on Thursday said she was left wanting more after the defense panel submitted only two names of witnesses it wants to present before…

blocks.text: House lead impeachment prosecutor Representative Gerville Luistro on Thursday said she was left wanting more after the defense panel submitted only two names of witnesses it wants to present before the impeachment court on December 1.
“Medyo nakakabitin (A bit lacking),” Luistro said in an ambush interview.
She also reiterated that Vice President Sara Duterte can best shed light on the allegations that came out during the impeachment trial.
The defense panel asked the impeachment court to subpoena Customs Deputy Commissioner Atty. Agaton Teodoro Uvero and Dr. Lourdes Tingson-Lebosada of Cale88 Foods Corporation.

Luistro said the prosecution had been hoping to receive the complete list of the defense's remaining witnesses, noting that the impeachment court had allotted four days, from December 1 to 4, for the defense's presentation.

“Sana if possible ma-disclose na lahat so that the impeachment court can strategize how to set the date for continuation of presentation of witnesses at yung mga succeeding pa na kailangan gawin for purposes of concluding this trial,” she said.

(Hopefully, if possible, they can disclose the complete list so that the impeachment court can strategize and determine the schedule for the continuation of the presentation of witnesses, as well as the subsequent proceedings that need to be undertaken to conclude the trial.)
Asked why the defense had submitted only two names, Luistro said there could be two possibilities: either the panel was having difficulty producing witnesses or it had no other witnesses to present.
“It's either they are having a hard time producing the witnesses or they really don't have witnesses," she said, adding that the prosecution hoped to see the complete list.
Luistro said that after the defense concludes its presentation of evidence, it will make a formal offer of evidence, which the prosecution will then have the opportunity to comment on.
The impeachment court will subsequently rule on the formal offer before the prosecution and defense deliver their closing statements.
The senator-judges will then vote on the verdict.

When asked how the testimonies of Uvero and Lebosada will impact the defense panel's presentation, Luistro replied, "Yung kay Dr. Lebosada, I think that will be a duplication of what has been testified to already by the previous witnesses. Ang ite-testify ba nila tungkol sa extent ng ownership, registration with BOI and FDA? Sana ang maging testimony nila, on the actual exportation. At pagdating naman dito sa BOC (deputy) commissioner, we look forward na talagang ma-substantiate nila yung alleged exportation ng Cale88."
Luistro said the prosecution panel will seek clarification from Lebosada regarding the P11 million check she received from Vice President Sara Duterte.

When asked why the defense panel seems to be concentrating on Cale88, Luistro replied, "Let us be reminded na ang specific allegation po ng prosecution dwells on the P817 million. This is unexplained wealth, undeclared property, and this Cale88 transaction is just a portion of the same. So sana ma-cover din yung malaking bahagi nitong unexplained wealth and undeclared property, which is the bulk, the substance, the core of the specific allegations of the prosecution."
The lead impeachment prosecutor maintained that Duterte can best answer the allegations.

"Meron na rin namang mga testigong nailatag ang defense. Talagang tayo nafu-frustrate because it does not address squarely the issues raised by the prosecution. And I really maintain my position, tanging si Vice President Sara Duterte lang ang may kakayanang ipaliwanag lahat ng allegations ng prosecution," Luistro stated.

"Palagi niyang sinasabi, she will answer in the proper forum. This is the proper forum. And I believe that this is the last opportunity, in as far as the impeachment process is concerned, para maipaliwanag niya ang kanyang sagot dito sa mga alegasyon ng prosecution. And as a Filipino citizen, hindi na bilang prosecution, I look forward to hearing the answer of the respondent herself," she added.
House impeachment prosecutor Rep. Terry Ridon shared this view.

"For example, doon po sa binabanggit ko lagi na 2023 SALN na walang P80 million pero like past P100 million po yung laman, yung bank, financial, investment at insurance accounts. Yun pong mga external witnesses relating to that like insurance and investment, baka too late in the day na maipasok pa ho sila. So makakapagpaliwanag na lang po talaga diyan, yun pong mag-asawang Duterte Carpio kung bakit yan hindi itinala sa kanya pong SALN for 2023," Ridon said in a separate interview.
"Tingin ko kung wala ho silang maipresenta to rebut the prosecution evidence. The prosecution evidence will, in fact, stand," Ridon added.
The Bicol SARO Party-list representative, however, emphasized the importance of Lebosada's testimony.

"Siyempre mahalaga po itong testimonya po ni Dr. Lebosada kasi siya po yung kalahati noon pong Cale88. Yung "CA" supposedly si Atty Carpio yon. Yung "LE," siya po yung Lebosada roon. So kung meron hong aktuwal na principal na puwede po talaga makapagpaliwanag ng lahat ng mga transaksyon, hindi lang po itong P700 million and yun pong unstated na P500 million doon po sa kanila pong mga transactions at yung China transactions, tingin ko malaki po yung puwede pong maipaliwanag ni Dr. Lebosada dito po sa bagay po na ito," Ridon explained.

When asked about the possibility of the defense panel presenting VP Duterte as a witness, Ridon replied, "If she will be presented there, she will obviously be subjected to cross-examination by the prosecution." —LDF, GMA News
